# Command-line reference

The same tables are available at run time, as JSON, from `rcp describe`.

## Commands

| Command | Arguments | Writes | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `SOURCE DESTINATION` | yes | copies a tree, recording every entry in a catalog |
| `resume` |  | yes | finishes the copy of the catalog named by -id |
| `sync` |  | yes | brings the destination of -id back in line with its source, removing what the source dropped |
| `isync` | `SOURCE DESTINATION` | yes | syncs without a catalog, comparing the two trees as they are |
| `verify` | `SOURCE DESTINATION` | no | compares two trees byte for byte and reports every difference |
| `scan` | `SOURCE` | no | lists a tree and reports its shape, optionally saving the listing as an index |
| `estimate` | `SOURCE` | no | projects how long a copy would take, from a measured sample |
| `delete` | `TARGET` | yes | removes a tree; counts only until -force |
| `chmod` | `TARGET` | yes | applies a mode across a tree |
| `chown` | `TARGET` | yes | applies an owner and group across a tree |
| `diag` | `SUBCOMMAND` | yes | the diagnostic family: file utilities, generated I/O, index diagnosis, find and change |
| `show` | `[HOST]` | no | the mounted filesystems here, or what an NFS server offers |
| `serve` |  | yes | the far end of an ssh:// endpoint, on stdio; takes no arguments |
| `indexlist` |  | no | the catalogs under the catalog directory |
| `indexdelete` |  | yes | removes the catalogs named by -id or -match |
| `logdump` |  | no | the job log; given an ID it also writes ID.zip in the working directory |
| `copybatch` |  | yes | copies one batch of files on a worker's behalf (-nodes) |
| `scanbatch` |  | no | scans one subtree on a worker's behalf (-nodes) |
| `job` | `start\|list\|status\|wait\|cancel\|log\|forget` | yes | runs a command in a session of its own and reports on it afterwards, so a caller need not wait for a terabyte; a canceled job leaves its catalog behind, which `rcp resume` finishes for a copy -- a sweeping verb (`sync`, `isync`) is finished by running that verb again, because `resume` never plans a removal |
| `mcp` | `[rails]` | no | a JSON-RPC 2.0 server on stdio, so an agent host can call rcp as a tool. The server writes nothing itself; each call runs rcp as a child, which carries this server's rails, so -readonly here makes every call read-only rather than refusing to start |
| `describe` |  | no | this description, as JSON |
| `help` | `[info\|filters]` | no | the usage text |
| `version` |  | no | the version, the transports and what this build's hardware offers |

## Endpoint schemes

| Scheme | Syntax | Writable | Sparse | Hard links | Symlinks | Xattrs | ACLs | Rename | Identity | Delta | Times | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `/path or file:///path` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | nanosecond | a local or mounted directory |
| `nfs` | `host:/export[:/sub] or nfs://host/export` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | nanosecond | an NFS export reached with the built-in v3 or v4.0 client |
| `ssh` | `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | nanosecond | a directory on a host that has rcp, through `rcp serve` over ssh |
| `rcp` | `rcp://host:port/path` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | nanosecond | the same `rcp serve`, over a socket it holds with -listen; plaintext, so the serve may bind only loopback |
| `rcps` | `rcps://host:port/path` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | nanosecond | the same socket inside TLS; with -tls.clientca the serve authenticates the peer, which is what lets it bind a routable address |
| `sftp` | `sftp://[user@]host[:port]/path` | yes | no | yes | yes | no | no | yes | no | yes | second | a directory on a host that has only OpenSSH, through its sftp subsystem |
| `s3` | `s3://bucket[/prefix]` | yes | no | no | yes | no | no | yes | no | no | nanosecond | an S3 bucket; POSIX metadata rides in user metadata |
| `hdfs` | `hdfs://namenode:port/path or hdfs:///path` | yes | no | no | no | no | no | yes | no | no | millisecond | an HDFS path over WebHDFS |
| `oci` | `oci://host[:port]/repository[:tag]` | yes | no | no | no | no | no | no | no | no | none | a container registry's repository as an OCI image layout |
| `tar` | `tar://ARCHIVE[!/SUBPATH]` | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no | no | yes | no | nanosecond | a tar archive as a tree: read any member, or write a new archive (ustar with pax headers, holes carried as GNU pax 1.0 sparse members); .tar.gz and .tar.zst are read by their magic and written by their name |
| `smb` | `smb://[user@]host[:port]/share[/path]` | yes | no | no | no | no | no | yes | no | no | 100-nanosecond | a Windows, Samba or NAS share over SMB2 (dialects 0x0202-0x0300, NTLMv2) |
| `dav` | `dav://host[:port]/path or davs://...` | yes | no | no | no | no | no | yes | no | no | none | a WebDAV collection (Nextcloud, SharePoint, Apache mod_dav) |
| `http` | `https://host[:port]/path or http://...` | no | no | no | no | no | no | no | no | no | second with rcp-index.json, none from an autoindex | a web server as a READ-ONLY tree, listed from rcp-index.json, an nginx JSON autoindex or an Apache HTML one |

## Options

| Option | Kind | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-parallel` | setting | worker count, or auto[:N] for the online tuner of workers plus read and write concurrency (default: CPUs, 2 to 8) |
| `-listen` | setting | serve: an address to serve the protocol on (loopback, unless -tls.cert, -tls.key and -tls.clientca are all set; -allow is required) |
| `-bs` | setting | read and write block size (default 1m) |
| `-engine` | setting | auto, uring or threads |
| `-depth` | setting | stop below this depth |
| `-bwlimit` | setting | read at most this many bytes a second (at least 4k) |
| `-nodes` | runs a program | comma-separated hosts to spread the copy or scan over |
| `-copybatch` | runs a program | a program to run per batch instead of copying here |
| `-dircount` | setting | NFS readdir buffer size (1k to 4m) |
| `-catalog` | safety rail | the catalog directory (else RCP_CATALOG, else the state directory) |
| `-newid` | setting | record this run under a new catalog id |
| `-id` | setting | the catalog id to resume, sync, scan from or delete |
| `-noid` | setting | keep no catalog for this run |
| `-snap` | path | resume or sync from this source instead of the catalog's |
| `-match` | setting | keep paths matching this glob (repeatable) |
| `-exclude` | setting | drop paths matching this glob (repeatable) |
| `-minsize` | setting | files at least this large |
| `-maxsize` | setting | files at most this large |
| `-newer` | setting | files modified within this age |
| `-older` | setting | files untouched for this age |
| `-type` | setting | f, d or l |
| `-uid` | setting | files owned by this user |
| `-gid` | setting | files owned by this group |
| `-fileid` | setting | the entry with this inode number |
| `-nohash` | setting | no digest in the catalog; the kernel may copy the bytes |
| `-sha256` | setting | digest with SHA-256 (the default) |
| `-blake3` | setting | digest with BLAKE3 |
| `-xxh3` | setting | digest with XXH3-64, the hash rsync and rclone speak; fast and NOT cryptographic |
| `-xxh128` | setting | digest with XXH3-128, the hash rsync and rclone speak; fast and NOT cryptographic |
| `-md5` | setting | accepted for compatibility; the run's digest is unchanged |
| `-delta` | setting | send a file the destination already has as a patch against it |
| `-compress` | setting | compress the payloads on an ssh:// or rcp:// stream |
| `-compress.codec` | setting | lz4 (fast, the default), deflate or zstd (slower, smaller on text); implies -compress |
| `-compress-codec` | setting | the same as -compress.codec, the spelling the first zstd change used |
| `-compress.level` | setting | how hard deflate works, 1..9 (default 6); needs -compress.codec deflate, since neither lz4 nor this crate's zstd encoder has a level; implies -compress |
| `-nolinks` | setting | copy hard links as separate files |
| `-noxattr` | setting | skip extended attributes and ACLs |
| `-acl4` | setting | carry NFSv4 ACLs on NFS endpoints |
| `-chown` | setting | ownership must be preserved: fail otherwise |
| `-noown` | setting | never touch ownership |
| `-preserve-atime` | setting | leave the source's access times as they were |
| `-fsync` | setting | flush every file to stable storage |
| `-nocache` | setting | drop what was written from the page cache |
| `-dryrun` | setting | plan and report, write nothing |
| `-force` | setting | actually remove (delete counts without it) |
| `-removetopdir` | setting | remove the top directory too |
| `-replace` | setting | overwrite what is already there |
| `-nodata` | setting | compare metadata only |
| `-noattrs` | setting | compare content only |
| `-nomods` | setting | ignore modification times |
| `-mtimewindow` | setting | tolerate this many seconds of modification-time difference |
| `-json` | safety rail | the run's events on stdout as JSON, one object per line; human lines move to stderr |
| `-allow` | safety rail | a root this run may touch, repeatable; outside it every endpoint is refused before it is opened |
| `-readonly` | safety rail | refuse every command that writes to an endpoint; rcp still records the run in the catalog's jobs.log |
| `-confirm` | safety rail | the plan digest a dry run printed; the run proceeds only if the plan still has that digest |
| `-requireconfirm` | safety rail | refuse a run that would remove or overwrite unless -confirm matches |
| `-v` | setting | one line per entry |
| `-l` | setting | the long listing |
| `-q` | setting | no per-entry output |
| `-stats` | setting | the statistics report |
| `-csv` | setting | report as comma-separated values |
| `-html` | setting | report as HTML |
| `-fmt` | setting | a format string per entry |
| `-du` | setting | report sizes as du does |
| `-duk` | setting | report sizes as du -k does |
| `-edupe` | setting | report duplicate files |
| `-hashcache` | setting | reuse a remembered digest when size, mtime and inode all still agree |
| `-rsyncable` | setting | cut .tar.gz members at content-defined boundaries, so an edit does not change every later member |
| `-nonames` | setting | numeric user and group ids |
| `-progress` | setting | a progress line on stderr every few seconds |
| `-noprogress` | setting | no progress lines |
| `-loglevel` | setting | INFO or DEBUG |
| `-all` | setting | show everything, not just the usual subset |
| `-h` | setting | the usage text |
| `-help` | setting | the usage text |
| `-version` | setting | the version and transports |
| `-V` | setting | the version and transports |
| `-sample` | setting | how many bytes to read for the rate sample |
| `-gbit` | setting | the link speed to project against |
| `-t` | setting | how long a live test copy may run, or how long `job wait` waits |
| `-user` | setting | the user to set |
| `-group` | setting | the group to set |
| `-user-from` | setting | only change entries owned by this user |
| `-group-from` | setting | only change entries owned by this group |
| `-reference` | path | take the mode or owner from this path |
| `-mode` | setting | the mode to set |
| `-rcp.remote` | runs a program | the rcp to run on an ssh:// host |
| `-via` | runs a program | an ssh://[user@]host[:port] or rcp://host:port whose rcp serve opens every remote endpoint of this run on its behalf |
| `-tls.ca` | transport | the PEM bundle an rcps:// client checks the serve's certificate against (default: the system bundle) |
| `-tls.cert` | transport | this side's certificate chain (PEM): what a serve -listen presents, and what an rcps:// client presents when asked |
| `-tls.key` | transport | the private key for -tls.cert (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1) |
| `-tls.clientca` | transport | the PEM bundle a serve -listen requires the peer's certificate to come from; naming it is what turns mutual TLS on, and what lets a serve bind anything but loopback |
| `-nfs.sec` | transport | sys, krb5, krb5i or krb5p |
| `-nfs.vers` | transport | 3 or 4 |
| `-hdfs.namenode` | service | the namenode for hdfs:///path |
| `-s3.endpoint` | service | the S3 service to talk to |
| `-s3.profile` | credential | the AWS profile to take credentials from |
| `-s3.insecure` | transport | use http when the S3 endpoint names no scheme |
| `-s3.noverify` | transport | skip certificate verification |
| `-oci.user` | credential | USER:PASSWORD for the registry |
| `-dav.user` | credential | USER:PASSWORD for the WebDAV server |
| `-smb.user` | credential | [DOMAIN\]USER:PASSWORD for the SMB share |
| `-smb.sign` | setting | sign and verify every SMB message even when the server does not ask, so an edit that clears its signing bit is refused |
| `-smb.handshake` | transport | seconds an SMB handshake may take before the connection is retried (default 10) |
| `-dav.insecure` | transport | use http for davs:// endpoints |
| `-dav.noverify` | transport | skip certificate verification for davs:// endpoints |
| `-http.user` | credential | USER:PASSWORD for an http:// or https:// source |
| `-http.noverify` | transport | skip certificate verification for https:// sources |
| `-http.index` | path | the published index to look for (default rcp-index.json; empty forces the autoindex readers) |
| `-oci.insecure` | transport | use http for oci:// endpoints |
| `-oci.noverify` | transport | skip certificate verification for oci:// endpoints |
| `-rmrf` | setting | diag: remove this tree |
| `-cat` | setting | diag: print this file |
| `-mkdir` | setting | diag: make this directory |
| `-rmdir` | setting | diag: remove this empty directory |
| `-rmid` | setting | diag: remove this catalog |
| `-n` | setting | the offset to read a job log from, and diag: how many |
| `-rand%` | setting | diag: percentage of random access |
| `-read%` | setting | diag: percentage of reads |
| `-npend` | setting | diag: how many operations in flight |
| `-size` | setting | diag: how large |
| `-u` | setting | diag: user |
| `-g` | setting | diag: group |
| `-umap` | path | diag: user id mapping, read from this file |
| `-gmap` | path | diag: group id mapping, read from this file |
| `-atime` | setting | diag: the access time to set |
| `-mtime` | setting | diag: the modification time to set |
| `-top-match` | setting | diag: match at the top level |
| `-branch-match` | setting | diag: match a branch |
| `-m` | setting | diag: a measure argument |
| `-j` | setting | diag: a job argument |
| `-read` | setting | diag: read |
| `-write` | setting | diag: write |
| `-random` | setting | diag: random access |
| `-sequential` | setting | diag: sequential access |
| `-wrdata` | setting | diag: write data |
| `-rebuild` | setting | diag: rebuild the index |

## Events

With `-json`, each line on stdout is one of these events.

| Event | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `entry` | a file, directory or symlink completed: path, kind (f\|d\|l), size, mtime_ns, mode, and digest when the run hashed it |
| `removed` | sync removed an entry the source dropped: path |
| `deferred` | the destination will remove the entry itself, later (a registry's garbage collector): path and why; not a failure |
| `kept` | the destination refused to remove the entry and it is still there (a lock, a namenode's no): path and why; the run fails |
| `difference` | verify found one: kind, path, detail |
| `warning` | something worth saying that did not fail the run: message |
| `error` | an entry or the run failed: code, message, and op and path for an entry |
| `done` | the command ended: status (passed\|failed), command, and that command's counts |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | the command passed (STATUS: PASSED) |
| 1 | the command failed (STATUS: FAILED); the events say what |
